claim: Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) is emerging as a revolutionary method for resolving the structure of macromolecular complexes in situ.
source: Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) is emerging as a revolutionary method for resolving the structure of macromolecular complexes in situ.
evidence: This is a general statement about the field supported by established scientific knowledge and the citation Beck and Baumeister, 2016 in the introduction.

claim: Sample preparation for in situ Cryo-ET is labour-intensive.
source: However, sample preparation for in situ Cryo-ET is labour-intensive and can require both cryo-lamella preparation through cryo-focused ion beam (FIB) milling and correlative light microscopy to ensure that the event of interest is present in the lamella.
evidence: This is a statement about the practical challenges of the technique, supported by general knowledge in the field.

claim: Sample preparation for in situ Cryo-ET can require both cryo-lamella preparation through cryo-focused ion beam (FIB) milling and correlative light microscopy.

claim: PIE-scope is an integrated cryo-FIB and light microscope setup.
source: Here, we present an integrated cryo-FIB and light microscope setup called the Photon Ion Electron microscope (PIE-scope) that enables direct and rapid isolation of cellular regions containing protein complexes of interest.
evidence: This is a direct description of the system presented in the manuscript.

claim: PIE-scope enables direct and rapid isolation of cellular regions containing protein complexes of interest.

source: Specifically, we demonstrate the versatility of PIE-scope by preparing targeted cryo-lamellae from subcellular compartments of neurons from transgenic Caenorhabditis elegans and Drosophila melanogaster expressing fluorescent proteins.

claim: The authors demonstrated the versatility of PIE-scope by preparing targeted cryo-lamellae from subcellular compartments of neurons from transgenic Drosophila melanogaster expressing fluorescent proteins.

claim: PIE-scope will increase the throughput and accuracy on projects requiring correlative microscopy to target protein complexes.

claim: Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) is currently the principal method for investigating the structure of proteins and protein complexes directly in their native environment.
source: Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) is currently the principal method for investigating the structure of proteins and protein complexes directly in their native environment (Beck and Baumeister, 2016).

claim: It is not possible to image a cell in regions thicker than 500 nm using a conventional 300 keV transmission electron microscope.
source: First, it is not possible to image a cell in regions thicker than 500 nm using a conventional 300 keV transmission electron microscope (Frank, 1996).

claim: The cellular environment is extremely heterogeneous and it is impossible to unequivocally identify every visible density.

evidence: This is supported by citations to Marko et al., 2006; Marko et al., 2007; Hsieh et al., 2014; Rigort et al., 2010.

claim: In a single lamella, only a portion of the cell is retained for cryo-ET but it remains unknown as to whether the protein/complex of interest is present.

claim: Every step from FIB milling to cryo-ET imaging is time-consuming.

claim: The solution to targeting has been correlative light and electron microscopy (CLEM).
